title: One page per repo: Waiting on you first, project status below, one writer ranks it
why: Your question and ruling, Oct 27 12:14 and 12:15 CDT (cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh2VxTQsRurAKzBZMkrCcNMRj, cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh28rSboTZRAZdREzMmGF34Lw, cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh2JTri9SaU6kmwj1ysw38q14): why two pages, and who ranks the questions?
note: Ruling, Oct 27 12:15 CDT (shiv): one writer per page ranks every item by severity and priority, and with one writer the status page (o8) and the waiting page (c71) merge into one artifact. One page per repo, owned by one writer: triage in this project, the orchestrator in a repo. "Waiting on you" comes first; project status sits below it or in a tab. Sessions send their questions to the writer and never write the page themselves (c126 builds that half). Your answers keep living in the page's storage, so a rebuild or a republish never loses them. The two-page proposal (separate pages that link to each other) is dropped. Next cloud lane: skills/roadmap and skills/waiting-page build one page from both data sets; the writer's ranking is a field it sets on each item; red first on a republish that would drop a saved answer. Due after: c126 and d9 merge, since they rewrite the same skill. Port: yes, every repo's page. Placed ahead of c135 (triage, Oct 27): it settles what c135 and c132 build on.
